newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Six Red Cross workers killed in Russia's Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Six Red Cross workers killed in Russia's Chechnya.

text.p: Six workers of the International Committee of the Red Cross, all of them foreigners, were killed in Russia's breakaway region of Chechnya on Tuesday, a spokeswoman for the organisation said.
"Six employees of the ICRC were killed this morning in (the village of) Novye Atagi," the Moscow-based spokeswoman said by telephone.
The spokeswoman did not give any other details and said an official statement would be issued later on Tuesday.
Russia's Itar-Tass news agency said the Red Cross workers were medical staff in a recently opened hospital in Novy Atagi, 17 km (11 miles) to the southwest of the capital Grozny.

Tass quoted Movladi Udugov, first deputy head of the separatist government of Chechnya as saying the incident, if confirmed, "would be a terrible link in a chain of provocations against the fragile peace process in Chechnya".

Both Moscow and Chechnya's separatist leaders are trying to keep the peace settlement on track in the region where tens of thousands of people were been killed in 21 months of fighting between Russian troops and the rebels.
